2011_024_062111regmtg.paragraph: The Troy School District Board of Education met in regular session on June 21, 2011 at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, opening with a public hearing on the proposed 2011/2012 budget presented by Assistant Superintendent for Business Services Mark Rajter. The packet carries the draft 2011-12 budget book, April and May 2011 treasurer's reports and check registers, May board minutes, three purchasing bid awards, administrative contract extensions, a first reading of the revised Code of Student Conduct, and the 2010-11 budget amendment and 2011-12 appropriations resolutions. The 2011-12 General Fund is appropriated at $128,282,487 against budgeted revenues of $127,175,517, built on a foundation allowance of $8,805.00 per pupil and a blended count of 12,106.00.

**Meeting.** Troy School District Board of Education, Regular Meeting, June 21, 2011, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district offices 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW). Agenda items: public hearing on the 2011/2012 proposed budget (Mark Rajter), recognitions, consent agenda A-I, personnel contract extensions, first reading of Code of Student Conduct revisions, 2010/2011 budget amendment, 2011/2012 budget appropriations resolution, facilities study update, Diversity Council report, a resolution supporting the Troy Public Library millage, and the year in review.

**2011-12 budget assumptions.** Projected blended student count 12,106.00, an increase of 74.78 FTE's from 2010/11; the membership formula changed from 75%/25% to 90%/10%, and without the change the blended count would have been 12,098.50 (7.50 less). Foundation allowance $8,805.00 per pupil, assuming a permanent $470.00 per-pupil decrease plus one-time offsetting revenues of $112/pupil and $100/pupil for a net reduction of $258.00. Retirement rate budgeted to rise from 20.66% to 24.46% on October 1, 2011; FICA unchanged at 7.65%. Budget reductions of $2,562,913 and revenue enhancements of $1,563,813, totaling $4,126,726 and 24.95 FTE, are included.

**Millage.** The 2011-12 appropriations resolution levies 18.0000 mills non-homestead operating, 11.4608 mills on commercial personal property, 5.4608 mills homestead and industrial personal property, and 4.70 mills on all classes for debt retirement. Estimated 2011/2012 homestead total is 16.1608 and non-homestead 28.7000. Taxable value falls from $3,886,391,481 to $3,562,981,820, labeled -8.32%.

**Resolutions and awards.** The 2010-11 amendment appropriates $138,268,519 (General Fund), $5,439,235 (Special Revenue), $18,598,717 (Debt Service), $7,216,120 (Capital Projects) and $109,208 (Internal Service). Bids awarded: trash removal to Allied Waste Services at $77,000 / $79,000 / $81,000 over three years; CAD workstations to Inacomp TSG at $65,790.00; custodial chemicals to Staples Business Advantage, not to exceed $75,000 per school year. Superintendent Dr. Barbara A. Fowler's contract is extended through June 30, 2014; four assistant superintendents and 27 administrators through June 30, 2013; Shawna Veit is appointed Supervisor, Special Education.

**Financial reporting.** April 2011 disbursements totaled $5,161,046.20 and May 2011 disbursements $7,019,343.22, with full Pentamation check registers, wire transfer and ACH debit schedules attached.
2011_024_062111regmtg.verbose:
Troy School District Board of Education, Regular Meeting, Tuesday June 21, 2011, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. District address 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, 248.823.4000; meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW), Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except July and August. Board membership: Nancy Philippart, President; Ida Edmunds, Vice President; Paula Fleming, Secretary; Gary Hauff, M'Liz Malven, Todd Miletti and Wendy Underwood, Trustees. Superintendent: Dr. Barbara A. Fowler.

**Public hearing, 2011-2012 proposed budget.** Item 2.A attaches a PowerPoint and the draft 2011-12 budget book; the report was presented by Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services. Taxable values fall from $2,360,627,214 homestead and $1,525,764,267 non-homestead in 2010-2011 ($3,886,391,481 total) to $2,212,203,470 and $1,350,778,350 in 2011-2012 ($3,562,981,820 total), a change labeled -8.32%. Student count calculations: September 2010 count 12,027.15; February 2011 count 12,060.98; estimated September 2011 count 12,111.00; February 2011 at 10% = 1,206.10; September 2011 at 90% = 10,899.90; 2011-12 student count 12,106.00, an increase of 74.78 FTE's over 2010/11 K-12 membership of 12,031.22. The pupil membership blend changed from 75%/25% to 90%/10%; without the change the blended count would have been 12,098.50 (7.50 less). Foundation allowance is $8,805.00 per pupil, assuming a permanent $470.00 per-pupil decrease and one-time offsetting revenues of $112/pupil and $100/pupil for a net reduction of $258.00.

**Assumptions.** Retirement rate budgeted to increase from 20.66% to 24.46% on October 1, 2011; FICA rate 7.65%. MESSA Pak rates are budgeted at fixed cost for single, 2-person and family plans under negotiated premium caps; MESSA covers the Troy Education Association (TEA) and Troy Educational Secretaries Association (TESA); Troy Education Support Personnel Association (TESPA) benefits are also budgeted at fixed cost. General Fund salary expenditures decrease $2,444,469 from the amended 2010/11 budget. Teachers receive 0.0% schedule increase with no step increases and a net decrease of 7.8 FTE's (+5.4 International Academy East, −13.2 eliminated positions); administrators 0.00% and a decrease of 3.35 FTE's; TESA a 3.00% salary decrease and a decrease of 1.4 FTE's; TESPA 0.00%; non-represented 0% and a decrease of 0.50 FTE. Indirect-cost transfers into the General Fund: Community Education Fund $587,349; Food Service Fund $131,091; Durant Fund $2,153; Troy Career Center $100,000; Grants $26,281. General Fund expenses exceed revenues by $1,106,970; projected General Fund balance at June 30, 2012 is $12,086,734, the Durant Fund balance remains $5,610,166, and the combined estimated total fund balance is $17,696,900. Athletics and Durant are reported in the General Fund beginning 2010/11; Troy Career Center grants move to a Special Revenue Fund in 2011/12; a new Capital Project Maintenance Fund is established for 2011/12.

**Budget reductions and revenue enhancements, "Items for Consideration 2011-12"** (draft dated 6/10/2011). Grand total 24.95 FTE and $4,126,726 for 11-12, $2,353,976 for 12-13, $200,000 for 13-14; split 13.20 certified and 11.75 non-certified, and by type $1,563,813 revenue and $2,562,913 expenditure. Items include reducing building supply budgets 10% ($76,800), eliminating/reducing administrative positions (3.35 FTE, $266,198), restructuring athletic offerings and transportation ($78,875), restructuring pay to participate ($70,000), closing an elementary ($627,763) and a middle school ($1,198,898) booked in 12-13, restructuring PACE (3.00 FTE, $210,189), increasing student/teacher ratios ($70,063 elementary, $350,316 secondary), schools of choice IB MYP ($217,069) and K-1 by 67 pupils ($581,744), reducing elementary and middle school media specialists ($140,126 and $84,076), a 5-tier bus route system ($360,000), a Community Ed Fund equity transfer ($1,200,000 phased $500,000/$500,000/$200,000), and increasing KinderPlus tuition from $3,000 to $3,450 ($150,000).

**General Fund detail.** 2011-12 recommended revenues by source: Local $43,653,734 (34.55%); State $71,934,988 (56.93%); Federal $3,118,235 (2.47%); Interdistrict $7,647,967 (6.05%); total revenues $126,354,924; total other financing sources $820,593; total revenues and other financing sources $127,175,517. Expenditures by object: Salaries $68,652,429; Employee Benefits $34,755,457; Purchased Services $13,479,401; Repairs and Rentals $829,854; Supplies and Materials $5,996,789; Capital Outlay $68,843; Other $3,997,561; total $127,780,334. By function: Elementary $28,127,777; Middle School $16,521,057; High School $23,915,980; Pre-School and Summer $106,538; Total Basic Programs $68,671,352; Special Education $10,598,108; Compensatory Education $4,306,122; Career and Technical Education $759,646; Total Added Needs $15,663,876; Adult/Continuing Education $457,887; Total Instruction $84,793,115; Total Pupil Support Services $9,642,016; Total Instructional Support $5,784,797; General Administration $2,045,860; School Administration $7,662,345; Business Services $1,591,947; Operations and Maintenance $8,511,813; Pupil Transportation $3,391,941; Total Central Services $3,058,669; Total Support Services $41,689,388; Community Services $1,235,001; payments to other governments/site acquisition/prior-year adjustments $25,000; total other financing uses $539,983; total expenditures $128,282,487. Summary page: budgeted revenues $127,175,517, budgeted expenditures ($128,282,487), deficit ($1,106,970), beginning fund balance July 1, 2011 $18,803,870, ending fund balance June 30, 2012 $17,696,900.

**FY2011-12 grants.** Adult Education Civics $20,000; Adult Education Family Literacy $120,000; Career Development Grant $60,238 (Oakland Schools); IDEA-Flowthrough $1,837,592; IDEA-Preschool $54,683; Michigan School Readiness $108,800; CTE Millage $70,080; Title I $460,305; Title II Part A $264,376; Title III $339,502; and, for the Troy Career Center, Workforce Investment Act $3,201,330 through the Oakland County Michigan Works! Service Centers.

**Other funds.** Food Service: revenues $3,325,333, expenditures ($3,177,983), surplus $147,350, beginning balance $692,840, ending $840,190. Troy Career Center: revenues and expenditures both $3,201,330, no fund balance. Community Education: revenues $2,161,787, expenditures ($2,395,839), deficit ($234,052), beginning $1,244,333, ending $1,010,281, with program columns for Continuing Education, CARE Co., PAL and TOTS. Debt Service: revenues $19,408,535, expenditures ($18,448,150), surplus $960,385, beginning $518,484, ending $1,478,869; 2011-12 principal $12,460,000, interest $5,790,650, other $197,500. The debt retirement schedule through 2025-26 totals principal $116,040,000.00 and interest $40,857,150.00, grand total $156,897,150.00 across the 2007 (Fund 307), 2006 (Fund 306) and 2004(B) (Fund 304) issues. 2004 Capital Projects: revenues $44,271, expenditures ($1,102,084), deficit ($1,057,813), ending $(0). New Capital Projects Maintenance Fund: transfers in $500,000, ending $500,000. Internal Service: $120,000 revenues and expenditures.

**History.** Enrollment headcounts run from 12,070 in September 2000 to 12,045 in September 2010, with a projected September 2011 total of 12,111. The ten-year millage history shows a 2011-12 projected homestead total of 16.1608 (State Education Tax 6.0000, Hold Harmless 5.4608, Debt 4.7000) and non-homestead total of 28.7000; industrial personal property totals 16.1608 and commercial personal property 22.1608; in 1993/94 all taxpayers paid 31.0674 mills for operating purposes. The five-year forecast projects ending General Fund balances of $12,086,734 (2011/12), $4,638,928 (2012/13) and ($4,691,264) (2013/14), combined with Durant $17,696,900, $10,249,094 and $918,902, with retirement rates of 24.46%, 27.37% and 28.37% and cumulative budget reductions of $43,485,585.

**Treasurer's reports and registers.** April 2011 (memo dated June 1, 2011, signed by Mark S. Rajter): General Fund $2,030,998.51, Grant Fund $2,862.01, Troy Career Center $210,766.69, total General Fund $2,244,627.21; special revenue funds $32,348.16; building and site funds $22,851.47; student activity $83,322.53; memorial scholarship $1,850.00; ACH debits $43,099.30; outgoing wire transfers $2,732,947.53; total disbursements $5,161,046.20 with prior period voids of $215.00. The April Pentamation check register (report ACCTPA21, accounting period 11/11) totals $2,384,999.37. May 2011: General Fund $3,349,316.96, Grant Fund $14,531.85, Troy Career Center $320,745.71, Community Education $51,162.84, Food Service $9,657.02, total General Fund $3,684,594.52; special revenue $60,819.86; debt funds $135,239.08; building and site $13,717.26; student activity $189,460.48; memorial scholarship $39,766.92; ACH debits $33,000.21; wire transfers $2,862,744.89; total disbursements $7,019,343.22, prior period voids $798.82. The May register (period 12/11) totals $4,123,598.12; Fund 101 alone totals $3,074,183.60. Largest single items include MESSA premiums of $1,158,269.62 (April) and $1,164,088.02 (May), Blue Care Network at $74,403.54 each month, Enviro Clean Services custodial billings, First Group America transportation, Integrys Energy Services, and Oakland Community College GM Orion training purchase orders in the Troy Career Center grant fund. The May YTD Summary Revenue and Expense Budget Report shows General Fund total revenue original budget $136,363,473 with actual $110,010,891 and $26,352,582 uncollected (19.33%), total expenditures original $135,897,825 with actual $111,569,152, encumbrances $14,842,915 and available budget $9,485,758 (6.98%), excess revenue over expenditures $465,648, and fund balance moving from $18,861,061 at July 1, 2010 to $19,326,709 at June 30, 2011.

**Minutes approved.** May 3, 2011 regular meeting (Resolutions 11-041 through 11-047), including the Outstanding Support Staff Award to custodian David Jones, recognition of 29 retirees, National Teacher Appreciation Week May 2-6, 2011, an iPad Challenge demonstration, a $29,117.00 award to Inacomp TSG for Troy Career Center computers, Baker Middle School masonry to M. J. Chisholm ($6,800) and lockers to Steel Equipment Company ($16,300); May 12, 2011 special meeting (11-048); May 17, 2011 special meeting (11-049 through 11-053), appointing Timothy Fulcher principal of Smith Middle School, Merri Lynn Colligan Director of Technology and Katherine Jagels Director of Special Education, and supporting the Oakland Intermediate School District budget under Section 624 of the Revised School Code; the May 17 workshop; and the May 18, 2011 special meeting (11-054) ratifying the TEA/MEA/NEA tentative agreement of May 17, 2011 for August 15, 2011 through June 30, 2013.

**Purchasing and personnel.** Memos from Frank E. Lams, Purchasing Consultant, recommend Bid #9710 trash removal to Allied Waste Services at $77,000 (2011/12), $79,000 (2012/13) and $81,000 (2013/14); Bid #9712 CAD workstations at Athens High School to Inacomp TSG at $65,790.00; and Bid #9714 custodial chemicals to Staples Business Advantage, not to exceed $75,000 per school year. Contract extensions: Dr. Barbara A. Fowler through June 30, 2014, continuing a 5% base salary decrease she volunteered in 2008-2009; Dr. Richard Machesky, Jan Keeling, Mark Rajter and Jasen Witt through June 30, 2013; 27 administrators through June 30, 2013 except James Johnson (June 30, 2012); and Shawna Veit appointed Supervisor, Special Education, on a two-year probationary contract effective July 1, 2011.

**Code of Student Conduct.** First reading of revisions to a document last revised April 2008, with a second reading set for July 12, 2011; committee members Machesky, Kocenda, Goss, Roncone, Gebbie and Hannon. Revisions add Chapter 5 (Technology) and Chapter 6 (Bullying and Harassment, including cyberbullying), change make-up time to one day for each day absent, move loitering to Level II and fighting to Level III, and lengthen Level II fighting suspensions from 3-5 days to 5-7 days. Jasen Witt is named Title IX and Section 504 Coordinator.

**Resolutions.** The 2010-11 budget amendment appropriates $138,268,519 (General Fund), $5,439,235 (Special Revenue), $18,598,717 (Debt Service), $7,216,120 (Capital Projects) and $109,208 (Internal Service), with General Fund ending fund balance June 30 of $18,803,870. The 2011-2012 appropriations resolution appropriates $128,282,487, $8,775,152, $18,448,150, $1,102,084 and $120,000 respectively, and levies 18.0000 mills non-homestead operating, 11.4608 mills commercial personal property, 5.4608 mills homestead and industrial personal property, and 4.70 mills on all classes for debt retirement. Michigan Department of Treasury Form 614 (L-4029), the 2011 Tax Rate Request due on or before September 30, 2011, is attached with instructions. Other items: the facilities study team timeline running May 2011 through February 2012; the Diversity and Inclusion Council report by Rosalind Cox of R&J Consulting Group, engaged in March 2009, whose council first met in September 2010 with thirty-eight members and has held six meetings; a resolution urging support for the August 2, 2011 Troy Public Library millage vote; recognition of Athens High School's SET SEG Educational Foundation 2011 Summer Leadership Camp Scholarship presented by Thomas Longhway; retirement recognition of Dr. Don Van Den Berghe, Principal of Wass Elementary School, for 29 years of service since July 7, 1982; and a closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(a).
